input.value: mock ExecutionContext with a fresh, empty AnnotationMap
consumer that invokes accept(builder) but does not modify the builder

cases.expected: AnnotationMap contains exactly one JsonNodeAnnotation whose evaluationPath equals validator.evaluationPath, schemaLocation equals validator.schemaLocation, and keyword equals validator.getKeyword(); no additional attributes are present.
cases.description: Verify that putAnnotation creates an annotation with the default fields when the customizer does nothing.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with a fresh, empty AnnotationMap
consumer that calls builder.withAttribute("customKey", "customValue") before returning

cases.expected: AnnotationMap contains exactly one JsonNodeAnnotation whose evaluationPath, schemaLocation and keyword are set as above and that also holds a custom attribute 'customKey' with value 'customValue'.
cases.description: Ensure that a customizer can enrich the builder and that the resulting annotation reflects those extra attributes.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with a fresh, empty AnnotationMap
consumer that throws new RuntimeException("boom") when accept(builder) is invoked

cases.expected: RuntimeException with message 'boom' propagates out of putAnnotation and the AnnotationMap remains empty (no partial annotation stored).
cases.description: Validate that an exception thrown by the customizer propagates and does not leave a partially built annotation in the context.

input.value: null
any consumer (e.g., builder -> {})

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown because executionContext is dereferenced.
cases.description: Check that passing a null ExecutionContext results in an NPE, confirming the method does not guard against null arguments.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with an empty AnnotationMap
consumer that calls builder.withEvaluationPath("/override") and builder.withSchemaLocation(new SchemaLocation("/overrideSchema")) and builder.withKeyword("overrideKeyword")

cases.expected: AnnotationMap contains exactly one JsonNodeAnnotation whose evaluationPath is "/override", schemaLocation is "/overrideSchema", and keyword is "overrideKeyword" (the values set by the customizer). No other attributes are present.
cases.description: Verify that the customizer can replace the default evaluationPath, schemaLocation and keyword supplied by the validator.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext whose AnnotationMap already contains an annotation with key equal to the builder's default key and value = JsonNodeAnnotation with keyword "oldKeyword"
consumer that adds attribute "newKey":"newValue"

cases.expected: AnnotationMap still contains a single entry for the same key; the old annotation is replaced by the new one that has the original evaluationPath, schemaLocation, keyword (from validator) and the added attribute "newKey":"newValue".
cases.description: Ensure that putAnnotation overwrites an existing annotation for the same location instead of creating a duplicate.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with empty AnnotationMap
a spy consumer that records the number of invocations; it simply calls builder.withAttribute("count","1")

cases.expected: The spy reports exactly one invocation of accept(builder); AnnotationMap contains one annotation with the added attribute.
cases.description: Validate that putAnnotation calls the supplied Consumer exactly once.

group: putAnnotation - customizer adds null attribute value

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with empty AnnotationMap
consumer that calls builder.withAttribute("nullKey", null)

cases.expected: AnnotationMap contains one JsonNodeAnnotation that includes the attribute "nullKey" with a null value (or the attribute is omitted if the builder discards nulls, but no exception is thrown).
cases.description: Check how the builder/annotation handles a null attribute value supplied by the customizer.

input.value: mock ExecutionContext whose AnnotationMap already holds two unrelated annotations
consumer that adds attribute "extra":"value"

cases.expected: AnnotationMap size becomes three (the two original entries remain unchanged and a new annotation is added). The new annotation has the expected default fields plus the extra attribute.
cases.description: Confirm that putAnnotation adds a new entry without disturbing existing unrelated annotations.
